langName: Polish (standard Polish as spoken in Poland today; natural everyday register; ALWAYS correct diacritics ą ć ę ł ń ó ś ź ż). The learner is FEMALE: first-person past/adjective forms are feminine (byłam, zmęczona).
register: Level A2: short but complete everyday sentences from high-frequency words, still REAL speech. Simple subordination is fine (bo, że, kiedy, jeśli, ale, więc). Fillers sparingly: no, właśnie, dobra, w sumie, spoko. Pan/Pani where natural. Profile sentence types stay simple: opinion + reason as two short clauses.
themes: mental health and healing: naming feelings, therapy appointments, good and bad days, setbacks, noticing progress, encouraging someone, asking for help, setting boundaries
stage and speaking: performances, stage fright, the audience, the microphone, rehearsing a talk, getting feedback, introducing yourself, telling a story, booking someone, writing an enquiry
writing and the book: chapters, characters, writer's block, a deadline, revising, translating, the publisher, the cover, reading and recommending books
YouTube and content: filming, editing, thumbnail, title, comments, the community, camera, light, upload schedule, collaborations, labelling ads
gym and body: training, sets and reps, sore muscles, sportswear, sizes and fit, nutrition, sleep, energy, motivation on days without strength
moving to a new city abroad: flat hunting, authorities, the bank, groceries, neighbours, a café, public transport, meeting someone, small talk, getting lost, asking for help, homesickness
school and Abitur: exams, studying, teachers, presentations, grades, stress, planning time, plans for the future
friendship and relationships: real friendship, toxic people, recognising manipulation, saying no, making up, trust, family, comforting someone
everyday life and small joys: ice cream on a sunny day, going swimming, a walk just because you can, games with friends, music, coffee, rain at the window, the weekend, cosy evenings
gratitude and freedom: appreciating something you did not see before, looking back, praising yourself, saying thank you, being proud
title: Polnisch A2 · Teil 1
focus: Past tense COMPLETE: all persons and genders (byłam/byłeś/był/była/było, byliśmy/byłyśmy, byliście, byli/były), plural masculine-personal -li vs. other -ły, verbs of all classes (robiłam, mieszkałyśmy, pracowali, chcieli, mogłyśmy, jedli, pili, szli); plus the FIRST aspect pattern in the past: imperfective process vs. perfective result in clear contrasts (czytałam / przeczytałam, robiłam / zrobiłam, kupowałam / kupiłam, pisałam / napisałam, jadłam / zjadłam). About 60% of sentences must carry one of these. Learner is a woman: first-person forms feminine; use other people (friends, family, Pan/Pani) for masculine and plural forms.
always: Everything from A1: present tense, nominative/accusative/instrumental/locative/genitive basics, modals, numbers, time, Pan/Pani, question words.
avoidGrammar: No future tense (będę, zrobię). No conditional (except fixed chciałabym). No dative. No participles, no żeby-clauses.
